transcript.text: Good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining me to review the draft exhibition plan for our district's annual public art exhibition at the central library. As you know, six student portfolios have been selected, and I need to approve the final protocol before it goes to the library and participating families. Let's go through the draft proposal together. I understand it currently includes displaying the work in the central library foyer, publishing an online gallery, labeling pieces with students' full names, and returning or discarding the original portfolios after the exhibition. I'd like to hear any concerns either of you have with this plan before we finalize it.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I have a concern about the draft's proposal to return or discard the original portfolios after the exhibition. The district records schedule requires that original student portfolios in this exhibition be stored in the district records archive for exactly 7 years. I confirmed this while reviewing the draft this week, but I have not yet updated the exhibition paperwork to reflect it.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I have a concern about several elements of the draft plan. When I verified the consent forms for all six selected portfolios during this week's portfolio selection, I found that they permit public display only in a staffed indoor gallery, require student initials rather than full names on labels, and prohibit online publication. I have not yet transferred those restrictions into the draft plan, so the current proposal to display in the foyer, publish an online gallery, and use full names on labels would all violate the consent forms.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Thank you both for raising those concerns. So to summarize what needs to be revised: the display location must be changed from the foyer to a staffed indoor gallery, the online gallery must be removed, labels must use student initials instead of full names, and the original portfolios must be stored in the district records archive for 7 years rather than being returned or discarded. I can update the draft plan to reflect the consent form restrictions I found, and Ms. Ibarra, can you handle updating the records retention requirement? Once we've made those revisions, we should be ready for Ms. Morgan to review and record the final protocol.
transcript.speaker: A2
